subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is referenced by Zalthir as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Grygum might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: guard chamber
fact: The guard chamber contains a zurkhwood table, three chairs, a side table, and a Sava game set on the table.
source_quote: It contains a zurkhwood table and three chairs, a smaller side table, and a Sava game set on the table

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is referenced by Imbros as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow.
source_quote: Ilvara might decide his fate should be precisely like Serith's

subject: the key
fact: The key had hung around Kalan Strongbranch's neck once.
source_quote: It had hung around Kalan Strongbranch's neck once

subject: the stolen sapphire
fact: The stolen sapphire carried a summoning working — it could pull an item to you, but only an item not in anyone's possession.
source_quote: The stolen sapphire carried a summoning working — it could pull an item to you, but only an item not in anyone's possession

subject: the poison book
fact: The poison book had a dead scholar and was the center of the murder investigation.
source_quote: There is a poisoned book and a dead scholar

subject: the Oak Tree Apothecary
fact: The Oak Tree Apothecary is between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, a treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak.
source_quote: The Oak Tree Apothecary, he said, between the Sea Warden's Tower and the House of Mechanus, a treehouse grown into the roots of an evergreen oak

subject: Leuwin
fact: Leuwin is a satyr druid, elderly and absent-minded, with a pet squirrel.
source_quote: A satyr druid named Leuwin, elderly and absent-minded, with a pet squirrel

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir said, 'Totally, totally,' in a voice that recorded everything.
source_quote: Totally, totally," Zalthir said, in a voice that recorded everything

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said, 'I can read it. A small divining touch — the least of the seeing-arts.'
source_quote: I can read it," I said. "A small divining touch — the least of the seeing-arts.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin said, 'Look, I'm just saying, if we solve the murder, we get any book in the place.'
source_quote: Look, I'm just saying, if we solve the murder, we get any book in the place.

subject: Daral
fact: Daral had the poison book and worked out someone wanted him to take the fall.
source_quote: He had the poison book. He'd worked out someone wanted him to take the fall.

subject: Fembris
fact: Fembris wanted to attend Grygum's debate in the Oval Theater.
source_quote: Fembris asked to leave. Our minder... wanted to attend a debate. Grygum's debate, as it turned out — a disputation in the Oval Theater

subject: Candlekeep
fact: Candlekeep is the world's most dangerous library.
source_quote: the world's most dangerous library

subject: the keep
fact: The keep has an active murder running through it.
source_quote: There is an active murder running through this keep.

subject: the dining room
fact: The dining room is where the meals were served, and where, if you were a poisoner, you'd have wanted to be.
source_quote: The dining room, for one. Where the meals were served, and where, if you were a poisoner, you'd have wanted to be.

subject: the research area
fact: The research area was suddenly full of rooms nobody would be watching.
source_quote: everyone was now headed toward the research area, which meant the keep was suddenly full of rooms nobody would be watching

subject: the Oval Theater
fact: The Oval Theater hosted Grygum's disputation on his new theology.
source_quote: a disputation in the Oval Theater on his new theology

subject: Janussi
fact: Janussi picked up the book at dinner, and at the time, it was wrapped.
source_quote: The book got picked up by Janussi at dinner. And at the time, it was wrapped.

subject: Kalan Strongbranch
fact: Kalan Strongbranch handed off the key rather than wear it, paranoid, maybe.
source_quote: Strongbranch handed his off rather than wear it. Paranoid, maybe.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool tried to help, an eye surfacing through the ooze, hopeful.
source_quote: Glabbagool tried to help, an eye surfacing through the ooze, hopeful

subject: Bookwyrm
fact: Bookwyrm herself was unable to politically afford to miss Grygum's debate.
source_quote: Bookwyrm herself unable to politically afford to miss it

subject: Kelemvor
fact: The followers of Kelemvor have made the point very clear, repeatedly, through their god's usual incomprehensible cryptic phrasing.
source_quote: The followers of Kelemvor have made that point very clear, repeatedly, through their god's usual incomprehensible cryptic phrasing.

subject: Bahamut
fact: Bahamut may or may not have been watching.
source_quote: Bahamut may or may not have been watching.

subject: the Underdark
fact: The Underdark teaches you that the people who kill you usually want it documented first.
source_quote: the Underdark teaches you that the people who kill you usually want it documented first

subject: Menzoberranzan
fact: A Menzoberranzan child should have closed the connection on reflex.
source_quote: a Menzoberranzan child should have closed on reflex

subject: the locket
fact: A locket from around the dead man's neck was taken, and we assume that inside that locket was the key.
source_quote: Some locket from around the dude's neck was taken. We assume that inside that locket was the key.

subject: the wrapping
fact: Daral was baffled we even asked about a magical seal. 'Why would I put a magical seal on the wrapping? It's a gift!'
source_quote: Why would I put a magical seal on the wrapping? It's a gift!

subject: the poison
fact: The poison turned black after the dead man's saliva mixed with it.
source_quote: When I mixed with his saliva, it turned black, okay?

subject: the summoning spell
fact: The summoning spell could retrieve an item through a keyed gem, provided you had the magic to call it.
source_quote: The summoning had been worked on a *different* key.

subject: the murder
fact: The murder involved a poisoned book, a stolen key, a stolen sapphire, and a dead scholar.
source_quote: There is a poisoned book and a dead scholar.

subject: the debate
fact: Grygum's debate on his new theology drew half the avowed and caused Fembris to abandon his post.
source_quote: Grygum's debate, as it turned out — a disputation in the Oval Theater on his new theology, with half the avowed already in attendance

subject: the gift-giving
fact: Daral dropped the book under the evergreen tree around 11am on Deadwinter's Eve, before rushing to the keeper's Tower.
source_quote: He'd dropped the book under the evergreen tree, next to the other gifts, around 11am on Deadwinter's Eve

subject: the search
fact: The search for the killer required looking for clear vials of poison, not black splashes.
source_quote: A vial of some sort of clear.

subject: the timeline reconstruction
fact: The timeline of the book's poisoning was critical: whether tampering occurred before or after Daral handed it over.
source_quote: the timeline of the book itself, whether it was poisoned before or after Daral handed it over.

subject: the key's magical test
fact: Daz tested the key with a divining touch and found it clean — not linked to the summoning spell.
source_quote: I took custody of the key, set my fingers to the cold iron of it, and let the spell read the object... The answer was no. The key was clean.

subject: the sapphire's purpose
fact: The sapphire was not decoration — it was the retrieval token for the summoning spell, requiring the same stone to store and recall.
source_quote: The sapphire isn't decoration: it's the retrieval token, and it has to be the *same* sapphire both to store and to recall.

subject: the gap in the account
fact: Daz could not resolve the connection between the gem, the key, and the murdered man — a pattern he could see but not name.
source_quote: I reached for it and came up with nothing. The pattern was there. I simply could not make it resolve... I will call it a gap in the account.

subject: the decision to prioritize the killer
fact: Thorin declared the priority was to find the killer, not who stole the key.
source_quote: And our priority is to find the killer, not who stole the key.

subject: the revelation of the poison's activation
fact: The poison only activated upon contact with a living thing's saliva — it was clear in vials and turned black after death.
source_quote: The stuff only wakes up when a living thing touches it.

subject: the abandonment of Fembris's post
fact: Fembris left his post to attend Grygum's debate, handing the party an hour without supervision.
source_quote: A keeper of the keep, leaving his post, to watch the orc argue dragons. I did not stop him.

subject: the handoff of the key to Daz
fact: The key was handed to Daz by the narrator, after having been held by Kalan Strongbranch.
source_quote: I handed it to Daz and let it become his problem.

subject: the revelation of the summoning's mechanism
fact: The summoning spell works by binding an item to a gem, and the item can only be retrieved if the gem is possessed and the caster has the magic to call it.
source_quote: Possess the gem and you possess the item, provided you have the magic to call it.

subject: the identification of Daral's motive
fact: Daral's motive was to prove he wasn't a murderer, and he offered to ward every gift if he survived the night.
source_quote: if he made it through the night, hint, hint, he'd see to it everyone wrapped their gifts right. Wards on every wrapping, the kind that bite the careless, for everyone.

subject: the discovery of the locket's contents
fact: The locket was assumed to contain the key, and its theft implied the killer intended to remove the key from the victim's possession.
source_quote: We assume that inside that locket was the key.

subject: the realization that the poison was not on the book
fact: The poison was not visible on the book because it activated only after ingestion, not on contact.
source_quote: Why did it turn dark, but it's not dark on the book? Because it goes black after you die.

subject: the naming of the gap
fact: Daz refused to call his inability to resolve the connection a failure — he called it a gap in the account.
source_quote: I will not call that a failure. I will call it a gap in the account.
